features.evidence: misspellings like 'Sofwtare' and 'gnireenignE'
features.name: Proofreading accuracy
features.description: This captures how free the letter is from distracting spelling or typing errors, which affects polish and credibility.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors distract from the content or make the letter feel careless.
Several noticeable errors appear, though the meaning remains clear.
Only a few minor slips appear and they do not materially hurt readability.
Virtually error-free copy that reads as fully polished.

features.evidence: fragment-heavy sections like 'Direct experience building with AI... Extensive Python experience...'
features.name: Document flow
features.description: This captures how smoothly the letter moves from background to fit to evidence rather than feeling pasted together or repetitive.

levels.descriptor: Ideas feel scattered or pasted together, with weak transitions or abrupt shifts.
The case is understandable but somewhat list-like, repetitive, or mechanically structured.
The letter has a clear progression and connects evidence to fit with reasonable flow.
The narrative is especially coherent, economical, and easy to follow from opening to close.

features.evidence: openings like 'Every security team... bottleneck' or 'software that guards other software'
features.name: Role motivation
features.description: This captures how specifically and convincingly the writer explains wanting this exact security engineering role rather than any software job.

levels.descriptor: Shows only generic interest in software or security work.
States interest in the role but with broad or familiar reasons.
Connects the role's actual mandate to the applicant's goals or past experience.
Makes a distinctive, memorable case for this exact role with a clear personal rationale.

features.evidence: phrases like 'improvements there are inherited by every team downstream'
features.name: Platform orientation
features.description: This captures whether the applicant is drawn to foundational work with multiplicative impact across many teams.

levels.descriptor: No real signal that the applicant values platform or company-wide leverage.
Mentions scale or infrastructure in general terms.
Explicitly values foundational work whose benefits spread across many teams.
Repeatedly frames impact in terms of downstream inheritance, centralization, or fleet-wide leverage.

features.evidence: lines like 'defaults, not documents' or 'remove friction for other engineers'
features.name: Developer enablement
features.description: This captures how strongly the letter frames security tooling as a way to help product engineers do the right thing easily.

levels.descriptor: Does not discuss developer users or ease of adoption.
Shows some desire to help other engineers but without much detail.
Explicitly emphasizes making secure behavior easier, default, or less manual for developers.
Shows strong empathy for internal users through ideas like defaults over documents, friction removal, or close proximity to tool users.

features.evidence: phrases like 'production-grade, typed, tested' or 'built to a higher standard'
features.name: Engineering rigor
features.description: This captures the extent to which the applicant emphasizes dependable, carefully engineered systems rather than vague implementation experience.

levels.descriptor: Provides little evidence of high operational standards beyond having shipped software.
Uses general language about correctness, care, or trustworthiness.
Gives concrete signals of rigor such as typing, testing, predictable behavior, or careful release practices.
Makes rigorous engineering a central theme and ties it directly to security tooling quality.

features.evidence: background summaries with 3, 5, or 7 years
features.name: Experience tenure
features.description: This captures total professional software experience relative to the role's baseline.

levels.descriptor: At or just above the minimum bar, typically 2-3 years.
Solid mid-range experience, typically around 4-5 years.
Clearly above the preferred bar, typically 6+ years.

features.evidence: claims of launching 2, 4, or 6 production services
features.name: Launch history
features.description: This captures the demonstrated volume of production systems the applicant has helped test, maintain, or launch.

levels.descriptor: Limited volume, such as 1-2 production services.
Moderate volume, such as 3-4 production services.
High volume, such as 5+ production services.

features.evidence: Bachelor's, Master's, or Doctoral degree
features.name: Academic attainment
features.description: This captures formal academic level, which varies across the letters and maps to the posting's preferred qualifications.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's level preparation.
Master's level preparation.
Doctoral level preparation.

features.evidence: statements like 'Go as my primary language' or 'Go back-end services'
features.name: Go centrality
features.description: This captures how central Go appears in the applicant's actual work rather than merely being listed as one language.

levels.descriptor: Go is mentioned but not shown as a central working language.
Go is described as primary, daily, or most-used.
Go is tied to clear backend or infrastructure ownership.
Go is central to concrete role-matching systems design, especially security or agent infrastructure.

features.evidence: phrases like 'Python became my workhorse' or 'My Python is production-grade'
features.name: Python depth
features.description: This captures the depth and production seriousness of the applicant's Python experience.

levels.descriptor: No Python evidence or only the faintest mention.
Python is mentioned but with little sense of depth or production use.
Python is clearly used in production for services, tooling, or automation.
Python depth is unmistakable, with production-quality practices or central ownership of Python-based systems.

features.evidence: LLM-backed features that had to behave predictably
features.name: AI deployment
features.description: This captures whether the applicant has applied AI in production settings and how much operational care they show around it.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is presented.
Mentions AI or LLM work in broad terms only.
Shows production AI experience plus some concern for trust, evaluation, or correctness.
Shows substantial production AI responsibility with explicit attention to failure modes, controls, or dependable behavior.

features.evidence: architectures with 'Python agents' bounded by 'Go services'
features.name: Agent architecture
features.description: This captures direct experience designing agentic systems rather than only mentioning AI or automation broadly.

levels.descriptor: No direct agentic systems experience is shown.
Mentions agents or autonomy without architectural detail.
Describes an agent setup with clear components, often Python agents plus Go services.
Shows end-to-end architectural ownership with explicit guardrails, permissions, auditability, or supervision.

features.evidence: automation that classifies, deduplicates, or routes vulnerability reports
features.name: Triage automation
features.description: This captures hands-on experience automating vulnerability intake and handling, which is central to the role.

levels.descriptor: No concrete vulnerability-handling automation is shown.
Expresses interest in reducing manual security work but no evidence of having built it.
States direct experience automating vulnerability intake or triage.
Explains concrete triage behavior or impact, such as classification, deduplication, routing, or measurable time saved.

features.evidence: security work like 'threat modeling' and 'code review for common vulnerability classes'
features.name: Assessment practice
features.description: This captures whether the applicant has actually performed security assessments and how concrete that practice sounds.

levels.descriptor: No concrete security assessment practice is described.
Mentions assessments, reviews, or security work only vaguely.
Names specific assessment activities such as threat modeling, code review, attack-surface analysis, or remediation validation.
Shows repeated, structured assessment practice and frames it as a substantive engineering responsibility.

features.evidence: examples like redesigning an in-memory index or replacing brute force with streaming computation
features.name: Algorithmic application
features.description: This captures practical use of data structures or algorithms to improve real systems rather than generic claims of knowledge.

levels.descriptor: No data-structure or algorithm evidence appears.
Claims strength in algorithms without a concrete example.
Provides one concrete example of using algorithms or data structures to improve a system.
Provides a concrete example with clear impact on performance, tractability, or system design.

features.evidence: credentials like 'CompTIA Security+' or 'OSCP'
features.name: Security certification
features.description: This captures third-party validation of security knowledge or hands-on offensive skill.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
Mentions a foundational credential such as CompTIA Security+.
Mentions a hands-on credential such as OSCP.

features.evidence: capture-the-flag events with near-top finishes
features.name: CTF practice
features.description: This captures ongoing adversarial security practice outside normal job duties.

levels.descriptor: No capture-the-flag or similar adversarial practice is mentioned.
Mentions occasional or general CTF participation.
Shows sustained or high-performing CTF practice, such as strong or near-top finishes.

features.evidence: maintaining an open-source project or sending patches upstream
features.name: Open-source ownership
features.description: This captures external engineering stewardship, from occasional contributions to maintaining software used by others.

levels.descriptor: No open-source work is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches or contributions.
Maintains a project or library with regular review or release responsibility.
Owns an open-source project with outside users, contributors, or a visible community.

features.evidence: side builds like a distributed scheduler versus a small habit tracker
features.name: Project ambition
features.description: This captures the technical ambition of personal projects mentioned in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned or the project is minimal in technical scope.
Mentions a small app or straightforward solo tool.
Mentions a substantial systems project, often infrastructure or distributed in nature.
Mentions an ambitious systems project with explicit hard problems like replication, failover, consensus, compaction, or delivery guarantees.

features.evidence: before-and-after claims like 'queue went from a dreaded chore' or 'hours of expert attention it returned'
features.name: Impact evidence
features.description: This captures how clearly the letter shows outcomes from the applicant's work rather than only responsibilities or interests.

levels.descriptor: Mostly lists interests or responsibilities with no clear outcomes.
Provides background counts but little evidence of what changed because of the work.
Shows at least one clear result or before-and-after effect.
Shows concrete, vivid, or measured outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to evaluate.
